statusText: The CME weekend halt covers eighteen of the twenty-four published hours and holds Tail at the floor of a closed venue. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, leaving the 22:00Z Sunday restart as the only slot carrying materially elevated conditional risk.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 13, still well inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: CME equity futures stay halted through eighteen of the twenty-four published hours, with no scheduled U.S. release anywhere in the window and a Saturday CENTCOM report of six-month-high Strait of Hormuz shipments trimming the supply premium that carried crude above $100
body:
Eighteen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final six contain the 22:00Z restart and its first five hours. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September at 20:00Z and the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25, up 0.59% on the session against a 29,648.00-29,993.25 range, so the final observed futures mark sat 76 points below the session high rather than at an extreme. Friday's cash marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67%, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The index tape was rotational rather than uniform - Broadcom rose 3% and Micron 3.9% while Meta fell 2.4% and Oracle 2% on debt-funded capital spending concerns - and the Dow closed 95 points lower even as the Nasdaq gained 0.7%. Across the week the divergence was wider still, with the Nasdaq up 2.6% against a 733-point Dow decline and the S&P 500 up 0.7%. That split internal picture is the reason no structural Tail amplifier is carried into this window: the last observed session was divided, not one-way, and Friday was in any case a quarterly triple-witching expiry.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and was re-verified at the primary source. The FOMC raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, citing inflation that remains elevated and a desire to support a timelier return to the 2 percent goal, while noting that uncertainty remains elevated owing in part to geopolitical developments. Treasury yields rebounded into Friday's close, with the H.15 release showing the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September. Against that, VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range, so the options market ended the week without stress pricing. Crude remains the pivotal cross-asset file: WTI settled at 100.30, down 1.58% and lower for a third consecutive session, with Brent at 103.87, yet WTI is still up 18.85% over the month because Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike and the Strait of Hormuz remains contested.

Weekend reporting has been de-escalatory at the margin. U.S. Central Command said on Saturday that oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz over the past fortnight reached a six-month high, that the primary transit lanes are clear of mines, and that more than one billion barrels of crude have moved out of the Persian Gulf over roughly two months. U.S. officials have separately framed the Saudi pipeline restart in days rather than weeks. Neither development can be priced while the venue is shut, which is precisely why the conditional risk in this window concentrates at the reopen rather than across it.

No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. The first Monday catalyst, Goolsbee's remarks at 10:30Z, sits beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday, with the Bank of Japan's hike to 1.25%, its highest policy rate since 1995, the standing conditional for Asian risk appetite. A Trump-Xi summit expected around 24 September is a later-week wildcard outside this window. Tail is therefore published at the closed-venue floor of 4 through the deepest part of the halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, and reaching a window high of 13 across the restart before easing through the Asian hours. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first eighteen slots before stepping down to 4 across the final six hours. Stress opened at 22, eased to a 21 plateau across four morning hours, drifted back through 22 and 23 to a 24 plateau, reached 26 late and eased to 25 in the final two hours. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence peaked at 82 early in the window and decayed steadily to a 72 trough as distance from the Friday tape grew, recovering to 75 in the final hour as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Eighteen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final six contain the 22:00Z restart and its first five hours. Cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, and the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, beyond its end; the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 06:00Z, 6 from 10:00Z, 7 from 13:00Z, 8 from 16:00Z, 9 from 19:00Z and 10 at 21:00Z, then reaches 13 across the restart and its first full hour before easing to 12, 11 and 10 through the Asian session - a drift that tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure, and one that stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every published hour. Mode is published as mixed only for the restart and the two hours after it, reflecting expected two-way price discovery against conflicting inputs: a Fed that hiked to 3.75-4.00% with crude above $100 against a 14.81 VIX and firm semiconductors.
